Brent crude extended its rally to $92.54/bbl, up 5.69% ($4.99) on the day — a second consecutive sharp move, ~10% over two sessions, as the Trump-Iran compensation stand-off (logged in yesterday's digest) keeps the Hormuz reopening unresolved.

EPFR's weekly Global Navigator report (published today, covering the week through 08-05) flagged "chipflation" — AI-infrastructure buildout costs feeding through into tech-goods and electricity prices — as a second inflation channel alongside oil, on record alongside a Fed minutes note that AI infrastructure development would likely sustain upward price pressure through higher tech-goods and electricity costs.

The EIA raised its own Brent forecast in today's Short-Term Energy Outlook, citing "continued severe constraints on Strait of Hormuz transits" as the reason it now expects more Middle East crude to stay shut in than it did last month.

Houthi missiles killed six aboard the Tanzanian-flagged cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab al-Mandeb strait — the first shipping fatalities linked to Yemen's Houthis since the war began in February — while, separately, US forces fired on a Panama-flagged vessel in the Gulf of Oman for allegedly trying to breach Washington's blockade of Iranian ports.

Named datacenter projects tracked under this frame include Stargate, Camellia, and Colossus, alongside hundreds of smaller sites.

summary.gist: This meta-thread reframes AI capex from who's spending to where roughly $750B actually lands, across chips, datacenters, power, and land.
